content: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) has outlined strategies to improve the quality of diabetes care. These include the following: 1. Expanding Team Roles: Within the diabetes care team, specific roles should be assigned to ensure more intensive management of the condition. This approach involves regular monitoring and check-ins, particularly for patients who require more comprehensive and individualized care. 2. Implementing Electronic Health Records (EHRs): The use of EHRs facilitates better tracking of patient data. This enables healthcare providers to identify patterns in diabetes management and pinpoint areas where improvements can be made, ultimately enhancing patient outcomes. 3. Reducing Financial Barriers: It is essential to ensure that patients have access to critical resources, such as diabetes education, routine examinations, and necessary medications, without the prohibitive burden of high costs. Addressing financial barriers can significantly improve adherence to care plans and overall health outcomes. 4. Telehealth Services: Expanding telehealth services increases accessibility to diabetes care, especially for individuals living in rural or underserved areas. This approach ensures consistent, high-quality care delivery through remote consultations and follow-ups.
